newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee seen in range but looking bearish.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee seen in range but looking bearish.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Robusta coffee futures should hold this month's range for the time being, but bearish chart indicators may soon start to pressure benchmark September lower, analysts said on Monday.
London's September contract has been content to drift in a relatively tight trading ranges between $1,700 and $2,000. Friday's range, for example, was just $45.
Technical analysts said the market was likely to hold its range for the present, but pressure from longer-term indicators suggested a bearish tone.
"Momentum indicators remain oversold while the longer-term moving averages are generally heading lower and are above the market," said Adrian Haylor, an analyst at Sucden.
"But the market is farily well balanced and in the short term the range will probably continue to hold."
But a close below $1,700 would be crucial and signal a possible slide down to $1,550, he said.
Traders called the market to open below Friday's close, with one suggesting as much as $30 lower and another saying he expected between $10 and $15 lower.
Resistance was pegged around $1,900, with the 20-day moving average at $1,884 as the initial upside barrier, followed by Thursday's high of $1,889.
Traders said activity in London was likely to remain dull as players were expected to continue rolling their July positions ahead of the first notice day on Tuesday.
Also, with Brazil escaping damaging frost so far and with funds moving out of coffee futures, the market looked set to test lower levels, they said.
U.S. certified coffee stocks rose to 31,292 60-kg bags as of May 9, a net change of 4,373 bags.
New York's Green Coffee Association also said stocks rose in May and stood at 1,977,000 60-kg bags at May 31, a change of 122,000 bags from April 30.
